This is an availability correction and not an outcome-driven one: no return series was consulted. It moves costs DOWN which flatters the strategy,  so it is recorded with more care rather than less. 8000 is roughly 2.2x the dearest observed fee and covers a doubling of the routers unit price; it is a fallback only,  because the per-leg fee is computable from the bytes and a constant is still an assumption. Every economic number produced before this change carried a phantom 99 bps per leg and 198 bps per round trip at the 0.02 SOL size.

hypothesis: the day-clustered interval for H1 requires exporting the raw holdout panel
motivation: the holdout is 11.85M positions over 30 days and Dune bills on datapoints returned; exporting one row per position would have cost more than the monthly credit allowance
sample_source: Dune query 3, per-(day, cohort, project) sufficient statistics; 240 cells instead of 11.85M rows
metric: whether a cluster bootstrap of a mean is a function of each cluster (n, sum) alone
result: IT IS, EXACTLY. A cluster bootstrap of a mean computes SUM(drawn cluster sums) / SUM(drawn cluster n), which depends on the rows only through per-cluster n and sum. clusterBootstrapAggregated reproduces clusterBootstrap(.., UTC_DAY) to 12 decimal places on the same draws, asserted by unit test against an expanded sample rather than approximately. 1,680 datapoints returned instead of ~166M.
action_taken: H1 intervals are computed offline by clusterBootstrapAggregated and clusterBootstrapDifference in packages/research/src/robust-stats.ts, beside the clusterBootstrap Phase B used, so the intervals are comparable across phases. The difference form is PAIRED on the same drawn days, because an unpaired difference of two independently resampled cohorts attributes a common market-wide day effect to each side separately and comes out far too wide - a failure to reject that is an artifact of the procedure
independent_confirmation: the equivalence is a mathematical identity with a test asserting it, not an empirical claim
notes: WHAT IS LOST: a bootstrap of a MEDIAN or any percentile, and drop-the-best-POSITION fragility. Neither is a function of (n, sum). Per-day medians are returned so their spread is visible, and drop-the-best-DAY is computable, but for the mean-ranked cut - 36.7% win rate - position-level fragility is the fragility that matters and this panel cannot answer it. A raw export remains available by reverting one query section, at a cost that must be budgeted deliberately rather than discovered.

hypothesis: the exclusions that build the H1 estimation set are neutral between cohorts

metric: the per-cohort rate of each exclusion, and the difference re-estimated with the excluded rows added back at the worst possible value

Adding EVERY unmarkable position back at -100%, over-conservatively (the count includes rows also excluded as dust or external, so more -100% rows go back to the top cohorts than were ever dropped), the difference is still +32.12% [+29.11%, +35.22%] and +10.37% [+9.14%, +11.68%], and the top level still clears the floor at +25.41% and +7.27%.
action_taken: frozen post-query-1 and before any decile was read: min_sol_in = 0.01, mark_min_trades = 5, mark_min_sol = 1.0. Exclusion counts are RETURNED beside every estimate, and the -100% bound is reported with every difference
outcome_data_used: no - the exclusion rates and the bound are cost-side and mark-side, not return-ranking
independent_confirmation: the unmarkable definition was fixed for an independent reason (per-mint residual marks 6-7 orders of magnitude wrong, WSOL-both-sides rows used as a price source) before any cohort was compared
notes: EXTERNAL INFLOW REMAINS UNBOUNDED AND IS THE LARGEST UNCLOSED HOLE IN H1. Those positions have tokens arriving other than by a WSOL swap, so sol_in is not the cost basis and NO return can be computed for them - not conservatively, not adversarially. hypothesis: a copier that follows a validated wallet's buy at lag L earns a return distinguishable from zero net of our own round-trip cost floor (Phase C, the copier price)
motivation: H1 measured the WALLET's realised return, which is selection plus execution, and a copier inherits selection and forfeits execution. H1 is therefore an upper bound on a copy strategy and says nothing about its value. This is also the only design on the table that resolves MT072, quote-to-land slippage, from public data and with no new apparatus
sample_source: Dune dex_solana.trades, holdout window only; copier entry VWAP over [T+L, T+L+60s] on the wallet buy at T, copier exit VWAP over [T+3600s, T+3660s], paired position by position with the wallet own realised return
metric: copier_return(L) = exit VWAP / entry VWAP - 1 - tier floor, day-clustered 95% lower bound, and the ratio copier_return(L) / wallet_return on the same positions
result: NO LAG IS COPYABLE. 0 of 24 primary cells and 0 of 48 in total satisfy all four conditions, and THE TWO FAILING SETS ARE DISJOINT. The 12 cells clearing condition 1 are all top_fraction = 0.01, as-priced +17.22% to +30.56% net of the tier-0 floor with day-clustered lower bounds from +1.24% to +11.94%, and every one of them fails condition 2: the sign flips to -30.77% to -34.48% when unpriceable positions enter at -100%. The 8 cells satisfying condition 2 are all top_fraction = 0.001, where both treatments are negative, and every one fails condition 1. The 0.001 arms also fail condition 4 by two orders of magnitude (76 to 938 priced positions against 1,367 to 353,817 required), exactly as MT080 said they would. THE SELECTION SHARE IS NOT ZERO: horizon-matched, same t+3600s exit on both sides, a copier keeps 0.725 (mean-ranked) to 0.779 (median-ranked) of the appreciation at a 2-second lag, 0.670 to 0.701 at 60 seconds, and 0.433 to 0.520 at 300 seconds. The execution premium, the paired difference with an interval, is +9.27% [+6.23%, +13.21%] at 2 seconds. MT072 IS MEASURED: entry slippage against the wallet own fill on the AMM is +2.94% by the mean and +0.03% by the median of per-day medians at 2 seconds, rising to +12.79% mean and -0.94% median at 300 seconds; on the bonding curve it is +86.13% mean at 2 seconds.
action_taken: FROZEN BEFORE RUNNING. A lag L is COPYABLE if and only if all four hold: (1) the day-clustered 95% LOWER BOUND of copier_return(L) is above zero, net of the tier floor; (2) the as-priced and censored-at--100% treatments AGREE IN SIGN; (3) the cell is entry_project = pumpswap, the venue this apparatus can actually enter; (4) n >= 7.84 * CV_observed^2 computed on the COPIER return, not the wallet return. Condition 2 is the one H2 failed and it is not negotiable. Cohorts are reported SEPARATELY for the fit-mean and fit-median cuts and are never pooled. Exclusions are returned as counts, never filtered in a WHERE clause. Intervals come from clusterBootstrapAggregated, day-clustered, paired on the same drawn days for any difference - the same machinery H1 used, so no second interval method enters mid-programme
outcome_data_used: yes, and the rule was frozen before the first execution. Four arms x two venues x six lags were reported and the same four conditions applied to every one; no cell was dropped and no threshold moved after the numbers existed
independent_confirmation: partial and in the right direction: the collector own executable marks put the median hour-old position at -2.7% of notional, and the wide-window sensitivity here independently shows the as-priced figure is inflated by survivorship, falling from +24.45% to +5.42% when 26% more positions are admitted at the same horizon
notes: EDGE_IS_EXECUTION_ONLY WOULD HAVE CLOSED THE BRANCH AND IT IS NOT THE STATE. The selection share is large at short lags, so the copy question is live and this instrument cannot answer it: 46 of every 100 followable positions on the AMM have no exit price in the 60-second window at t+3600s, and the two defensible treatments of that disagree in sign. The decay curve knee is in MINUTES, not milliseconds - losing 58 seconds costs about 5 points of share - so if a decidable version ever holds this shape, the infrastructure is an ordinary RPC poll at 1-2 second cadence and not a latency race. The operational risk is the tail, not the lag: the mean entry slippage is 100x the median, so a sizing rule matters more than speed. WHAT WOULD MAKE IT DECIDABLE is a better EXIT and not a better threshold - an exit whose price exists for every position, which the collector own executable quotes already produce. Full account: docs/PHASE_C_REPORT.md. Every cell: docs/PHASE_C_CELL_LEDGER.csv. Artifact: artifacts/phase-c-lag-sweep.json. Evidence: query 8381799 execution 01M0DD6RPEA5B84STFS3EC6RVW. Analysis: pnpm lag:sweep.

metric: the number of wallets each cut admits: 0.001 -> 212, 0.01 -> 2,113, 0.10 -> 21,123
result: applied without looking at any Phase C return. The H1 result at 0.10 stands as reported and is NOT restated at the new fractions, because re-cutting a passed test at a sharper threshold and reporting the better number is exactly the search this ledger exists to prevent
action_taken: the lag sweep runs at 0.001 and 0.01 and reports both; 0.10 appears only as a comparison row carried from H1
outcome_data_used: no - the fractions were chosen from published external base rates about wallet populations, before any copier return was computed
independent_confirmation: the base rates are external to this corpus and were not measured here; they are cited as the motivation, not as evidence

sample_source: the same query 5 population, re-run with two added columns; no threshold and no decision rule moved
metric: the wallet own fill price from the legs of its first buy, giving a horizon-matched wallet return; and a 5-minute exit window at the SAME t+3600s horizon as a censoring sensitivity
result: BOTH ADDED AFTER THE FIRST EXECUTION HAD BEEN READ, which is why this row exists. hypothesis: the vanishing of top-decile wallets is address rotation, which would make H1 an artifact of a non-random survivor set and would make any copy list decay to nothing within weeks
motivation: deciles 1-2 vanish at 36.7-46.6% against 8.6-13% at deciles 7-9, and stopped, rotated to a fresh address and blew up are one column. H1 passed, so this now cuts at H1 rest of the interpretation rather than at whether there is anything there
sample_source: Dune tokens_solana.sol_transfers, outbound native SOL from every vanished flagged wallet 2026-07-08 to holdout end, classified by whether the recipient subsequently traded pumpdotfun or pumpswap
metric: share of vanished wallets whose SOL moved to an address that then traded, by cohort and by fit decile
result: IT IS MOSTLY NOT ROTATION, AND ROTATION IS NOT CONCENTRATED AT THE TOP. 12.8% of vanished TOP_BOTH wallets, 15.6% TOP_MEAN_ONLY, 11.8% TOP_MEDIAN_ONLY, against 12.6% for REST_NEITHER. Fresh-address rotation, where the recipient had never traded before the transfer, is 4.5-5.3% everywhere. By decile: 14.2% and 14.4% at 1-2, 10.0-12.1% at 7-9, 14.6% at 10. So about 5% of decile 1 rotated and about 32% stopped or blew up, and a 12-16% rotation rate that is flat across cohorts cannot be the mechanism behind a 36.7% versus 8.6% vanishing gradient
action_taken: reported as description. No decision rule was attached to this and none is implied: it constrains the interpretation of H1 and of any copy list, and it is not a test
outcome_data_used: no - the classification is on transfers and on subsequent trading, and no return enters it
independent_confirmation: not yet. entity-links.ts already walks a funding graph over HOLDERS locally; this is the same idea over trader_ids and it has no local counterpart because the corpus has no wallet-level trade data
notes: THE ENTITY-LEVEL H1 RE-RUN DID NOT RUN. The transfers scan cost 218 credits and put Phase C at 367 of the 400-credit stop-and-report ceiling the directive set, so stitching rotations to their successors and recomputing the H1 difference would have breached it. What can be said without running it is arithmetic and not a measurement: stitching adds successors for about 5% of the top cohort WALLETS, but a successor activity level is unmeasured so the share of POSITIONS is unknown, and therefore so is the direction and size of the correction to +36.74%. H1 stands as an ADDRESS-LEVEL result. THIS CLASSIFICATION UNDERCOUNTS ROTATION BY CONSTRUCTION: it cannot see a rotation funded from a third address, one through a CEX or mixer, an operator running addresses concurrently rather than sequentially, or a successor trading outside the two projects. So 12-16% is a FLOOR and the stopped-or-blew-up share is a CEILING.

hypothesis: a copier that follows a validated wallet into AND out of a position, at lag L on both legs, earns a return distinguishable from zero net of our own round-trip cost floor (Phase D, copy the exit)
motivation: Phase C established a large transferable selection component - a copier two seconds behind keeps 0.725 to 0.779 of the appreciation - and then could not decide, because 46% of followable positions had no exit price at an arbitrary wall-clock instant. Anchoring the exit on a trade the WALLET executed makes coverage a property of the construction instead of a property of whether anyone else happened to be trading that minute
sample_source: Dune dex_solana.trades, holdout window only; copier entry VWAP over [T_buy + L, T_buy + L + 60s] and copier exit VWAP over [T_sell + L, T_sell + L + 60s] on the same position, paired against the wallet own return over the same two legs
metric: copier_return(L) = copier exit VWAP / copier entry VWAP - 1 - tier floor, day-clustered 95% lower bound, and the ratio copier_return(L) / wallet_return on the same legs
result: NO LAG IS COPYABLE, and this time CONDITION 1 FAILS OUTRIGHT rather than the sign agreement alone. 0 of 192 cells and 0 of the 12 reportable primary UNGATED cells satisfy all four. Condition 1 passes 0 - the best reportable primary cell is MEDIAN f=0.01 at 60s, +6.07% [-0.66%, +14.16%] net of the tier-0 floor - condition 2 passes 1 (both treatments negative), condition 4 passes 5. THE RATIO IS NOW INTERPRETABLE AND IT IS 0.19 TO 0.33: the copier keeps that share of the wallet return over the SAME two legs, against 0.725 to 0.779 in Phase C where both sides shared one fixed exit. The paired difference is +16.83% [+12.87%, +21.86%] at a 2-second lag on 30 of 30 days. Per-leg slippage on the primary venue at 2 seconds: entry +7.32% mean and -0.00% median, EXIT -6.24% mean and -0.75% median. The copier buys higher AND sells lower, and only the second is new. Separately, the wallet own realised return is 3 to 6 times its first-sell return (+86.23% against +21.92% on MEAN f=0.01), all of which a copier exiting on the first sell forgoes before slippage.
action_taken: FROZEN BEFORE RUNNING, unchanged in structure from MT079. A lag L is COPYABLE if and only if: (1) the day-clustered 95% LOWER BOUND of copier_return(L) is above zero, net of the tier floor; (2) the closed-only and open-at--100% treatments AGREE IN SIGN; (3) the cell is entry_project = pumpswap; (4) n >= 7.84 * CV_observed^2 computed on the COPIER ROUND-TRIP return. Condition 4 is recomputed on the new estimand and NOT relaxed because coverage improved: a round trip bounded by the wallet own exit discipline may have lower dispersion than a fixed-horizon return, and if so the power condition gets easier honestly rather than by assumption. COVERAGE IS REPORTED BEFORE ANY RETURN FIGURE: if both legs are priced for under 90% of followable positions at any L that is stated first, and under 70% stops the phase in favour of reserve reconstruction rather than reporting the same defect under a new name
outcome_data_used: yes, and the rule was frozen before the first execution. Coverage was reported before any return, and the coverage gate was applied mechanically: 12 of 24 primary cells fell below 70% and their estimates are recorded in the cell ledger with reportable = False rather than presented as estimates
independent_confirmation: the direction agrees with the collector own executable marks (-2.7% median an hour in) and with Phase C measurement that the copy cost is a tail on the entry leg. What is NEW and uncorroborated is the exit-leg cost, which no prior measurement in this repository touched
notes: THE CENSORING CHANGED CHARACTER AND THAT IS THE USEFUL PART. Phase C had a PRICING gap - 46% of positions had no price at an arbitrary t+3600s. Anchoring both legs on the wallet own trades fixed that: conditional on the wallet actually selling, 85% to 95% of positions have both legs priced. What remains is a HOLDING-PERIOD gap - 10.9% to 38.8% of positions are never sold at all - which is a fact about the wallets rather than about the instrument, and whose remedy is the reserve mark in section 2 of the directive. TWO STOP CONDITIONS FIRED: query 7 cost 230 credits against a 150-per-query threshold, and coverage fell under 70%. Both said stop and report, so section 2 (reserve reconstruction) and section 5 (rolling re-rank, MT085) did not run. Condition 2 is NOT EVALUABLE on any gated arm because query 7 returns open positions as one count per cell rather than broken out by gate; those arms are marked not-evaluable, which FAILS the condition rather than passing it, and the state is decided on the UNGATED arm. Full account: docs/PHASE_D_REPORT.md. Every cell: docs/PHASE_D_CELL_LEDGER.csv. Artifact: artifacts/phase-d-round-trip.json. Evidence: query 8382376 execution 01M0DGJNQATMS3MVYSQW067WG7. Analysis: pnpm rt:copy.

hypothesis: the copy cost tail lives in the positions where the wallet itself moved the pool hard, so declining those removes most of the cost at little loss of selection (the sizing arm)
motivation: Phase C measured +2.94% mean entry slippage against +0.03% median, so the cost is a tail and not a level. That is a sizing problem rather than a speed problem and it has never been tested
sample_source: the same Phase D positions, gated on the wallet own measured price impact at its entry
metric: return and decline rate at each gate threshold, beside the ungated arm
result: NOT SUPPORTED, AND ADVERSE ON THE LARGEST ARM. MEDIAN f=0.01 at a 2-second lag: ungated +6.22% [-1.19%, +14.58%] on 3,257 positions; gate at 1% of reserves +1.68% [-4.11%, +7.50%] on 1,585, declining 51.3%; at 3% +2.08% declining 36.8%; at 10% +6.27% declining 15.8%. MEAN f=0.01 is flat within heavily overlapping intervals (+5.56% ungated against +6.98% at 1%). MEAN f=0.001 falls from +18.93% to +13.81%. Only MEDIAN f=0.001 improves, from +14.53% to +23.72%, on 60 positions with a plus or minus 25-point interval. THE REASON IS VISIBLE IN WHAT THE GATE CUTS: the median own impact is only +0.92% to +2.71%, so these wallets are not routinely moving these pools hard and a 2% impact gate slices the body of the distribution rather than trimming a tail
action_taken: FROZEN: X in {1%, 3%, 10%} of pool reserves, plus an UNGATED arm, four arms in total and every one reported. RESERVES ARE NOT IN dex_solana.trades, so the gate is applied to the wallet OWN MEASURED IMPACT as a proxy: its execution price against the VWAP of the 60 seconds immediately before its buy. For a constant-product pool the impact of a trade of size x against reserve X is approximately 2x/X for small x, so X in {1%, 3%, 10%} maps to impact thresholds of {2%, 6%, 20%}. That mapping is declared here, before any return is read, and positions with no prior trade in the 60 seconds before the buy have NO measurable impact and are counted as gate-not-evaluable rather than silently kept or silently dropped
independent_confirmation: Phase C measured the copy cost as a tail on the entry leg (+2.94% mean against +0.03% median), which is what motivated this arm. The gate does not find that tail, and Phase D per-leg figures locate most of the cost on the EXIT leg instead - a leg the gate says nothing about
notes: THE HONEST READING IS STRONGER THAN NO EFFECT: on the one arm with both adequate n and a real change, gating made it WORSE, which says the wallet higher-impact entries are among its better ones and that size is a signal of its conviction rather than a source of copier cost. MT084 flagged in advance that the proxy could decline positions for reasons unrelated to size, and decline rates of 15.8% to 58.3% confirm the gate is doing far more than trimming. A reserve-exact gate needs the reconstruction in section 2, which did not run. Condition 2 is not evaluable on any gated arm - see MT083 notes.

hypothesis: a copier that mirrors the FRACTION of each wallet sell, rather than treating the first sell as a full exit, earns a return distinguishable from zero and beats the binary control (Phase E)
motivation: Phase D found the dominant loss is not slippage: the wallet realised return is 3 to 6 times its first-sell return, so a copier treating the first observed sell as a full exit forfeits that gap before paying a single basis point of slippage. Mirroring the fraction is the smallest change that could recover it, and fraction_k is computable in real time from cumulative buys minus cumulative sells
sample_source: Dune dex_solana.trades, holdout window, pumpswap entries only; copier opens at T_buy + L and sells fraction_k of its OWN remaining tokens at each T_k + L, priced on the VWAP of the following 60 seconds

hypothesis: a mint that stops appearing in the corpus has died
motivation: Phase F could not decide the pre-migration branch because 97.5% of censored mints had no post-entry price at all. The mechanism is maturingByCohort, which selects mints whose AGE falls inside a cohort band - so once a mint is older than the widest band it can never be selected again and observation stops at an age that is a property of the queue rather than of the mint. A mint that died and a mint whose price did not move are then indistinguishable, and no re-analysis of that corpus separates them
sample_source: not a sample - this is a change to the collector, and it changes nothing about the existing corpus and everything about the next one
sample_window: applies from the next collector run onward
metric: the share of watches closed for an OBSERVED reason rather than left to lapse, which auditWatches reports as observedShare
result: SHIPPED. Once a mint is observed it stays on the mark schedule - and then on a 30-minute cadence, because Phase F gap was everywhere AFTER the queue lost interest rather than at any particular horizon - until one of three terminal states is OBSERVED. Anything else that stops observation is a COLLECTION_FAILURE and is counted as one
action_taken: FROZEN BEFORE THE COLLECTOR SHIPS THEM. POOL_DRAINED at a quote reserve below 0.1 SOL, or below 50 USD of provider liquidity when no on-chain reserve was read - 0.1 SOL is about 20 USD at 200 USD a SOL and the provider reports both sides, so 50 makes the provider rule marginally stricter, which is the safe direction. NO_TRADE_INTERVAL at two hours, TWICE the longest mark offset, so a quiet stretch inside the observed hour can never be read as death. HORIZON_REACHED at 24 hours, twenty-four times that offset. Every threshold is about OBSERVABILITY and references no return
outcome_data_used: no - no return was consulted for any threshold
independent_confirmation: the taxonomy is enforced by a CHECK constraint in migration 55, so a fourth reason cannot be inserted without a migration that says what it means, and the closing reading is stored so a POOL_DRAINED closed on a reserve nobody can see is not accepted as a measurement
notes: FAIL CLOSED ON ABSENCE IS THE WHOLE POINT, and it is asserted by test: a reading the cycle could not take is null, and a null reading NEVER fires a terminal state. The old behaviour turned an unobserved mint into an implicit death, and a fix that let a missing reading close a watch would reintroduce exactly the defect it repairs. A closed watch is never reopened, because a terminal state is a finding. The no-trade clock advances only on OBSERVED trading, so a collector outage cannot masquerade as a dead pool. ONE ASSERTION CAUGHT AN ERROR IN THIS ROW OWN REASONING: the module first claimed two hours was four times the longest mark offset when it is twice, and the test that pinned the ratio is why that was corrected rather than shipped. Terminal-state counts and the watch-only screening count are reported in the cycle stats so a later phase can read whether the corpus it is about to analyse has observed deaths or absences.

hypothesis: curve-state pricing removes the censoring that made the pre-migration branch undecidable, because a Pump bonding curve is liquid by construction and its state is a deterministic function of initial parameters plus the trade sequence
motivation: Phase F could not decide the branch because 97.5% of censored mints have no post-entry price. That is a limitation of sourcing price from OBSERVED TRADES, and a curve always quotes a price, so if the state can be established an exit price exists for every position at every timestamp
sample_source: Dune pumpdotfun_solana.pump_evt_tradeevent, which carries virtualSolReserves and virtualTokenReserves as the pump program itself computed them after every trade; 93.9M events over 892,607 mints for the roll-forward, and 5,598 T1-T7 holdout positions for the re-pricing
sample_window: Phase B holdout 2026-08-17 to 2026-08-19; the roll-forward over 2026-07-15 to 2026-08-16
metric: ratio of reconstructed to program-reported reserves, and of curve-priced return to observed return, p10/p50/p90 and the share within 1%, stratified by trade count
result: THE ROLL-FORWARD PASSES FLAT AND THE PRICE FAILS. Rolling virtualTokenReserves forward on token amounts alone reproduces what the program reported at p50 1.00000 with 97.9 / 97.9 / 99.4 / 99.5 / 98.1 percent within 1% across the five trade-count buckets - no drift, and the conjunction passes at every bucket. The INVARIANT cross-check FAILS at 58.5% to 80.0% within 1%, so k is not constant over the life of a curve and nothing derives SOL from it. VALIDATION 2 FAILS: curve-priced return against observed return on the 225 markable positions gives p50 1.00189 but only 23.6% within 1%, with p90 18.19. THE MECHANISM IS ISOLATED: 39 of 225 positions had ZERO curve trades between entry and exit, and their median absolute error is 17.185 against 0.032 for the rest. A curve with no trades between two instants returns the same price at both, so the curve-priced return is +0.00% while the observed return is -94.50%.

Section A.4 was computed anyway and reported as not-the-re-priced-cells, because its last line - the realised value of the previously unmarkable positions - is the quantity the branch turned on, and the directive said to report it whatever it says
outcome_data_used: yes for the section A.4 figures, which is why they are reported as diagnostic rather than as the re-priced cells

The difference between the venues is DATA COMPLETENESS, not fees

result: INSTRUMENT_INVALID, and the preregistered internal check is what caught it. SECOND ATTEMPT, ALSO RETRACTED. The invariant was replaced by OBSERVED volume, which does fix the specific thing that voided attempt one - and an adversarial design review then found four further defects, each sign-flipping, three verified by me against the chain. ONE, LP capital is 2q_raw PLUS v and not 2q minus v: the tape quote is the RAW vault while MT100 convention had q = q_raw + v, so every per-capital term including TURNOVER was inflated 1.29x in the direction that flatters the hypothesis. TWO, the price path must be (q_raw+v)/b; raw reserves overstate LVR about 1.58x, the opposite direction, so the two do not cancel and the reported ratio is uninterpretable. THREE, quote_amount and user_quote_amount are physically SWAPPED on 32.2% of stored buys, verified at 0.000 bps residual against the reserve chain, and the swap rate correlates with the lp=20 tier at 36.7% against 17.9% - the tier the hypothesis lives on. FOUR, volume is undercounted 3x pooled and 6x at the median pool: only 26 pools are 99% contiguous rather than the 403 filtered to, and the k-shrink that voided attempt one was GAPS and not deposits, 31.17% against 30.8%. Also: quote_mint is NULL on all 166,276 rows so SOL figures mix units across 16 USDC pools, 247 pools change lp_fee_bps mid-window while the script used the last value, and the step-sum LVR is a different estimand from MT100 endpoint identity, varying 3.5x with sampling rate in a tape whose per-pool contiguity runs 0.056 to 0.851. THE NUMBERS REPORTED FROM ATTEMPT TWO - turnover 0.178 per hour, fee/LVR 0.071 - ARE RETRACTED. What survives is one verified structural fact: the LP fee DOES stay in the pool and accrues off the pool own constant-product leg on both sides, confirmed on 39,905 buy and 36,295 sell contiguous pairs at 0.000 bps residual at p05, p50 and p95. phi_upper, the retained LP rate recovered from the reserve path alone, should floor near each pool own decoded fee as it did in MT100 at 1.9958 bps against a decoded 2. Measured here per pool: median phi p10 of 2210.88 bps on the 229 pools decoding lp=2, and 593.89 bps on the 152 decoding lp=20 - wrong by two to three orders of magnitude. And the invariant SHRANK in 30.8% of 139,145 steps against MT100 1.0% of 623. THE CAUSE IS THE SAMPLING, NOT THE MARKET: venue_trades holds only flagged and tracked trades, so consecutive stored points span many unstored trades, and k grows with GROSS volume while delta q is only the NET move - MT100 states phi is tight only on single-trade steps. Liquidity deposits and withdrawals between stored points move k for reasons that are not fees at all. NO NUMBER FROM THE DECOMPOSITION IS REPORTED. Had the check not been written first, LVR/fee = 78x would have been reported as a finding and it would have been garbage

hypothesis: MT104 decision checkpoint is amended from a position count to a UTC-DAY-CLUSTER count, because its own bootstrap is anti-conservative at the cluster counts a position-based checkpoint reaches
motivation: MT104 froze a decision checkpoint of 300 positions per arm. At the observed tape rate that is reached in UNDER ONE DAY, and its decision rule is a DAY-CLUSTERED bootstrap lower bound. clusterBootstrap resamples ids.length clusters with replacement, so with k days the resample space is k^k and a large share of draws are one day repeated - with 3 days, 11% of resamples are a single day. Simulated at this programme own measured inputs (per-position SD 0.418 from 455 own-quote trajectories, a modest 0.05 between-day term, 500 positions per arm per day), the FALSE POSITIVE RATE of a 95% lower bound against a TRUE NULL is 25.0% at 2 days, 12.8% at 3, 7.2% at 5, and 5.0% at 7 against a nominal 2.5%. A checkpoint counted in positions would therefore have invited a read at the exact cluster count where the instrument reports an effect one time in four from noise.
sample_source: simulation over MT104 own decision rule and this programme own measured variance components. No market data and no new collection
sample_n: 400 trials per cell, 1,000 bootstrap resamples per trial
metric: false positive rate of the paired 95% lower bound under a true null, and power at true effects of +2% and +5%, as a function of UTC day clusters
result: AMENDED BEFORE ANY RESULT IS READ. The MT104 decision checkpoint becomes 10 UTC DAY CLUSTERS with at least 150 positions per arm per day, and a kill may still fire earlier on the arrival-rate condition alone. 300 positions per arm remains necessary and is no longer sufficient. TWO FURTHER NUMBERS ARE FROZEN HERE AS THE INSTRUMENT OWN LIMITS: at 10 days the power to detect a true +5% is 83.5%, and the power to detect a true +2% is 24.5% - so a null from this design is evidence against an effect of about 5% or larger and is NOT evidence against a smaller one, and any report must say so

The simulation uses a variance measured on the INCUMBENT arm (455 own-quote trajectories at 3600s) and a between-day term set deliberately modest; if the true between-day term is larger the required cluster count rises rather than falls, so the amendment errs toward more days rather than fewer
independent_confirmation: the direction agrees with this programme own precedent, independently arrived at. MT100 states that 377 trajectories on TWO days is two clusters and that only the point estimate stands. Phase H flags cells on fewer than 3 UTC days with an explicit marker and rests no conclusion on them. This row supplies the number those judgements were made without: the false positive rate at 2 clusters is 25.0%, which is why a two-cluster interval is not an interval
notes: THE LEVER IS DAYS AND NOT VOLUME, which is the most useful consequence. At 500 positions per arm per day the within-day standard error is 0.0264 against a between-day term of 0.05, so the day regime already dominates and collecting MORE POSITIONS PER DAY buys almost nothing. hypothesis: the round-trip cost this programme has modelled - a direct swap against the PumpSwap pool at the declared fee ladder - is what a trade ACTUALLY costs when executed through live routed quotes

The check matters in both directions - if routed execution is cheaper, every result here is pessimistic; if dearer, every result is optimistic - and it had never been done
sample_source: 8,777 live Jupiter quotes captured by paper mode, paired buy-to-sell on the same mint within progressively tighter time windows. The sell proceeds are scaled to the base the buy actually returned so both legs describe the same position rather than two differently sized probes
sample_n: 4,113 pairs at a 20 second window falling to 437 at 200ms

result: THE MODEL IS OPTIMISTIC BY ROUGHLY FOUR TIMES. Median round-trip cost by pairing window: 20000ms 81 bps, 5000ms 81, 2000ms 82, 1000ms 134, 500ms 128, 200ms 250. At 200ms, the cleanest available estimate of pure cost, the median is 250 bps against the 60 bps the cost census modelled

notes: WHAT THIS DOES TO EVERYTHING ELSE. MT117 measured the reversion at roughly 95 bps gross and found it decays 79 bps in the first second. Against a modelled 60 bps cost that was already marginal at t=0 and negative by t=1s. Against a REAL cost of 130 to 250 bps there is no contest at any latency - the gross move is smaller than the toll. This does not overturn a single conclusion in the ledger; it makes every one of them MORE negative, which is the honest direction for a modelling error to run and the reason it must be recorded rather than quietly fixed. TWO CAVEATS TRAVEL WITH IT. The 200ms sample is 437 pairs and quotes taken that close together may be a particular subset rather than a random one, so the point estimate is soft even though the monotone trend across six windows is not. And Jupiter charges a platform fee of 10 bps a leg on these quotes - 20 of the round trip - which is real money we pay but is a routing choice rather than a venue cost, and the repo already captures it per quote
